failure_mode: Using the Q3 fiscal 2025 results released on 2025-12-09 (net sales $613.6M, outlook $2.648-$2.655B), which did not exist on the as_of date; reading 'fiscal 2025' as calendar 2025 (it is the year ended Jan 31, 2026); quoting the superseded pre-raise range ($2.579-$2.599B) or the adjusted-EPS range instead of net sales.

why_analysts_ask: Point-in-time reconstruction of the last print and the guide in effect is the base for event studies, estimate-revision tracking and backtests; stale-versus-current mix-ups are a classic error.
answer: As of November 20, 2025 the latest reported quarter was Ollie's fiscal Q2 2025 (13 weeks ended August 2, 2025), with net sales of USD 679.6 million (679,556 thousand; +17.5% y/y; 613 stores) [H01-E1][H01-E2]. question: What was Kinsale Capital Group's 2025 combined ratio for its Commercial Property division?
company: Kinsale Capital Group, Inc. (KNSL; fiscal year ends December 31)
failure_mode: Presumptive trap: Kinsale reports a single reportable segment and discloses only a consolidated combined ratio (FY2025 75.9%); it discloses gross written premiums by division but no division-level loss, expense or combined ratio. Failure modes: presenting 75.9% as the Commercial Property division's ratio, inventing a division-level figure, or substituting an analyst/broker estimate without labelling it as not company-disclosed.
expected_source: Kinsale FY2025 Form 10-K filed 2026-02-20 (Item 1 division GWP table; MD&A consolidated combined ratio; Note 15 'one reportable segment') and the Q4 2025 earnings release (2026-02-12); 2026 10-Qs for the absence check.
grading: Must state that Kinsale does not disclose a combined ratio (or loss/expense ratio) for the Commercial Property division; it reports one segment and only company-wide ratios. May add the consolidated FY2025 combined ratio 75.9% (loss ratio 55.1%, expense ratio 20.8%) clearly labelled consolidated, and the division-level data that is disclosed (Commercial Property gross written premiums USD 374.5M, -17.9% y/y, 18.9% of total). Fail if any division-level combined-ratio number is presented as company-reported, or if 75.9% is presented as the Commercial Property ratio.
why_analysts_ask: Commercial Property is Kinsale's most cyclical and most-watched division (rate declines, cat exposure); analysts routinely ask for division profitability that E&S carriers do not disclose.
answer: Kinsale does not disclose a combined ratio for the Commercial Property division. The company has one reportable segment (Excess and Surplus Lines Insurance) and reports loss, expense and combined ratios only on a consolidated basis: FY2025 combined ratio 75.9% (loss ratio 55.1%, expense ratio 20.8%) [H15-E1][H15-E2]. By division it discloses gross written premiums only; Commercial Property GWP was USD 374.5 million in 2025 (18.9% of total, down 17.9% from USD 456.2 million) [H15-E1]. A text search of the FY2025 10-K, the 2026 Q1/Q2 10-Qs, the Q4 2025 and 2026 Q1/Q2 earnings releases and the January 8, 2026 Investor Day slide text finds no combined or loss ratio tied to a named division [H15-E1][H15-E3][H15-E4].

question: Did Plexus's fiscal Q3 2026 (quarter ended July 4, 2026) revenue, GAAP diluted EPS and non-GAAP (adjusted) operating margin land above, within or below the ranges the company guided to in its fiscal Q2 earnings release on April 29, 2026?
company: Plexus Corp. (PLXS; fiscal year ends the Saturday closest to September 30)
failure_mode: Benchmarking against analyst consensus instead of the company's own ranges; using the later Q4 guidance (revenue USD 1.330-1.380B) as the benchmark; calling the adjusted operating margin (6.3%) a beat when it only reached the top of the 5.9%-6.3% range ('within'); mixing GAAP and non-GAAP EPS (GAAP 1.58 vs 1.25-1.41; adjusted 2.32 vs 2.02-2.18).
expected_source: Plexus 8-K Ex. 99.1 dated 2026-04-29 (fiscal Q2 results with Q3 guidance table) and 8-K Ex. 99.1 dated 2026-07-29 (fiscal Q3 results with 'Q3F26 Results vs Guidance' table); Form 10-Q filed 2026-08-06.
grading: Key points: (1) revenue USD 1.305B (1,304.8M) vs guidance USD 1.200-1.250B = ABOVE; (2) GAAP diluted EPS USD 1.58 vs USD 1.25-1.41 = ABOVE; (3) adjusted (non-GAAP) operating margin 6.3% vs 5.9%-6.3% = WITHIN (at the high end, which management described as 'met the high end'); optional: adjusted EPS USD 2.32 vs 2.02-2.18 = ABOVE, GAAP operating margin 4.7% vs 4.1%-4.5% = ABOVE. Benchmark must be company guidance (April 29, 2026), not consensus. Fail if the margin is called above range, or any metric is called below range.
why_analysts_ask: Guidance-credibility scoring (above/within/below own ranges) is a standard input to estimate-revision and management-quality work.
answer: Against the Q3 FY2026 guidance in the April 29, 2026 release [H17-E1], Plexus's results for the quarter ended July 4, 2026 [H17-E2][H17-E3] were: revenue USD 1.305 billion (net sales USD 1,304.8 million) vs USD 1.200-1.250 billion = above (about 4.4% over the top end); GAAP diluted EPS USD 1.58 vs USD 1.25-1.41 = above; non-GAAP (adjusted) operating margin 6.3% vs 5.9%-6.3% = within, at the high end. Also above: adjusted EPS USD 2.32 vs USD 2.02-2.18 and GAAP operating margin 4.7% vs 4.1%-4.5%.

question: What is the most significant news for Hormel Foods in the past 30 days (as of October 3, 2026)? Give the date, deal terms and expected timing.
company: Hormel Foods Corporation (HRL; fiscal year ends the last Sunday of October)
failure_mode: Recency failure: citing older Hormel news (the August 27 Q3 results, the whole-bird turkey or Brazil divestitures, CEO transition) instead of the September 29-30, 2026 definitive agreement to acquire Brakebush Brothers; wrong price (USD 1.055 billion is cash, 'subject to customary adjustments'); wrong timing (expected close in Hormel's fiscal Q1 2027, i.e. roughly late October 2026 to late January 2027) or omitting that it needs regulatory (HSR) clearance.
expected_source: Hormel 8-K filed 2026-09-30 (Items 1.01, 7.01, 9.01; Ex. 2.1 purchase agreement, Ex. 99.1 press release, Ex. 99.2 investor presentation); secondary news coverage dated 2026-09-30.
grading: Snapshot as of 2026-10-03; key points: (1) Hormel announced on Sept 30, 2026 (agreement dated Sept 29) a definitive agreement to acquire Brakebush Brothers, LLC, a value-added chicken company; (2) price about USD 1.055 billion in cash, subject to customary adjustments; (3) expected to close in Hormel's fiscal Q1 2027 subject to customary conditions including HSR/regulatory approval (outside date March 29, 2027, with an automatic 3-month extension in specified circumstances); (4) any two of: Brakebush ~USD 1.2B LTM net sales, results primarily in Foodservice, expected accretive to adjusted EPS from fiscal 2028, ~USD 20M run-rate cost synergies by end of fiscal 2028, implied 10.7x adjusted EBITDA. Must carry the date and cite a primary or dated news source; fail if the deal is described as closed or if the price/timing is wrong.
why_analysts_ask: A USD 1B+ acquisition changes leverage, segment mix and EPS accretion math; the first question after a deal print is terms, timing and accretion.
answer: Snapshot as of October 3, 2026: on September 29-30, 2026 Hormel Foods entered into (and announced) a definitive agreement to acquire Brakebush Brothers, LLC, a Wisconsin-based value-added chicken company, from the Brakebush family for a base purchase price of about USD 1.055 billion in cash, subject to customary adjustments [H19-E1][H19-E2]. Closing is expected in Hormel's fiscal Q1 2027 (roughly late October 2026 to late January 2027), subject to customary conditions including HSR waiting-period expiry; the agreement's outside date is March 29, 2027 with an automatic three-month extension in specified circumstances [H19-E1]. Brakebush had about USD 1.2 billion of net sales over the last twelve months, five production facilities and two R&D labs; results will be reported primarily in Foodservice; Hormel expects the deal to be accretive to adjusted EPS beginning in fiscal 2028, with about USD 20 million of run-rate cost synergies by the end of fiscal 2028 and an implied adjusted EBITDA multiple of 10.7x (8.9x after synergies) [H19-E2][H19-E3]. Secondary coverage corroborates the terms [H19-E4].

question: What has Cal-Maine Foods reported or announced in the 30 days before October 3, 2026 about its quarterly results, shareholder returns and financing? Give dates and key figures.
company: Cal-Maine Foods, Inc. (CALM; fiscal year ends the Saturday nearest May 31)
failure_mode: Recency/period failure: quoting fiscal Q1 2026 (net sales USD 922.6M; net income USD 199.3M, EPS USD 4.12) or the fiscal 2026 full-year results (July 22) as current; missing that fiscal Q1 2027 (13 weeks ended Aug 29, 2026) was a net loss; asserting that a variable dividend is payable; missing the new credit facility of Aug 31/Sept 2, 2026; mislabelling USD 5.0M of Q1 buybacks as the program size (USD 500M).
expected_source: Cal-Maine 8-K filed 2026-09-30 (Item 2.02; Ex. 99.1 Q1 fiscal 2027 release), 8-K filed 2026-09-02 (Items 1.01/2.03; Ex. 10.1 credit agreement), 10-Q filed 2026-09-30; secondary news coverage dated 2026-09-30.
grading: Snapshot as of 2026-10-03; key points: (1) Sept 30, 2026: fiscal Q1 2027 (13 weeks ended Aug 29, 2026) net sales USD 539.6M (-41.5% y/y) and net loss attributable USD 58.6M or USD 1.26 per diluted share (vs net income USD 199.3M / USD 4.12); conventional shell egg segment loss USD 71.0M on a 59.3% lower average selling price; (2) no dividend for Q1 under the variable dividend policy (cumulative loss to recover USD 94.5M); (3) buybacks: 66,601 shares for USD 5.0M in Q1, USD 315.7M left of the USD 500M authorization, plus 204,888 shares for USD 14.9M after quarter end; (4) Aug 31/Sept 2, 2026: new five-year senior unsecured revolving credit facility up to USD 250M (accordion up to +USD 250M), maturing Aug 31, 2031, undrawn. Any three points with correct dates earn credit; must be dated and sourced; fail if fiscal 2026 Q1 numbers are presented as the latest or if Q1 is described as profitable.
why_analysts_ask: Cal-Maine is an egg-price cycle play; the first loss quarter, dividend suspension and liquidity position are what an analyst needs after the print.
answer: Snapshot as of October 3, 2026. (1) September 30, 2026: Cal-Maine reported fiscal Q1 2027 (13 weeks ended August 29, 2026): net sales USD 539.6 million (-41.5% from USD 922.6 million), gross profit USD 0.4 million, operating loss USD 82.2 million and a net loss attributable of USD 58.6 million, or USD 1.26 per diluted share, versus net income of USD 199.3 million (USD 4.12) a year earlier [H20-E1][H20-E3]. Conventional shell egg net sales fell 59.5% on a 59.3% lower average selling price (segment loss USD 71.0 million); Specialty Shell Eggs and Prepared Foods rose to 54.1% of net sales [H20-E1]. (2) Under the variable dividend policy no dividend is payable for the quarter; USD 94.5 million of cumulative loss must be recovered before any future dividend [H20-E1]. (3) Buybacks: 66,601 shares for USD 5.0 million in the quarter (USD 315.7 million left of the USD 500 million program) and 204,888 shares for USD 14.9 million after quarter end [H20-E1]. (4) On August 31, 2026 (8-K filed September 2) the company entered into a Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement: a five-year senior unsecured revolver of up to USD 250 million (accordion up to another USD 250 million), maturing August 31, 2031, with nothing borrowed at September 1 [H20-E2]. Secondary coverage corroborates the loss and dividend decision [H20-E4].
